article_title: The Effects of the 3-2-1 Reading Strategy on EFL Reading Comprehension
citation: Hashem Ahmed Alsamadani. (2011). The Effects of the 3-2-1 Reading Strategy on EFL Reading Comprehension. English Language Teaching, 4(3). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v4n3p184
title: The 3-2-1 reading strategy
description: The 3-2-1 strategy is an active, multi-strategy reading routine used while or after reading a text. Students first "summarize and cite three different major points or details they found while reading the passage", then share two of the three interesting items they identified, and finally write one question about the text and discuss it with peers. In this study the researcher modeled the steps to the experimental group, and students practiced the strategy for 30 minutes at the start of each roughly 100-minute reading class before completing book exercises.
requirements: Teacher modeling of the three steps until students understand how to use them
Time within regular reading classes for students to read, summarize, share, and discuss
constraints: In this study it was tested with low-intermediate Saudi EFL college students over six weeks; it did not significantly improve summarization ability
examples: Students individually read, summarized, shared, and discussed the reading for 30 minutes at the beginning of each class, then completed book exercises in small groups
key_sources: Hashem Ahmed Alsamadani. (2011). The Effects of the 3-2-1 Reading Strategy on EFL Reading Comprehension. English Language Teaching, 4(3). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v4n3p184

article_title: Percutaneous tracheostomy simulation training for ENT physicians in the treatment of COVID-19-positive patients.
citation: Favier V., Kimmoun A., Gatin A., Gallet P. (2020). Percutaneous tracheostomy simulation training for ENT physicians in the treatment of COVID-19-positive patients. European Annals of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Diseases. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anorl.2020.06.002
title: 3-hour simulation training module for percutaneous tracheostomy in COVID-19 patients
description: A 3-hour half-day session for 4-6 ENT trainees working in pairs, combining a 15-min video introduction presenting the kit and procedure steps, hands-on handling of a percutaneous tracheostomy kit, practice on a low-tech simulator, and four full-scale scenarios of increasing difficulty on a SimMan 3G mannequin with group debriefing. The authors state: "We designed a 3-hour training module, and here provide a step-by-step schedule, including video analysis, a demonstration of the kit, the recommended precautions related to COVID-19, and several simulation scenarios of increasing difficulty."
requirements: A simulation room equipped with video camera and microphones, a SimMan 3G mannequin, a facilitator (anaesthetist) and 1-2 session leaders
constraints: The number of persons present is kept to an absolute minimum for COVID-19 precautions, with other trainees watching a retransmission in an adjacent room
target_learners: ENT physicians called on to perform percutaneous tracheostomy in ICU
target_learning_goals: Perform percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy safely and efficiently in COVID-19-positive patients, including COVID-19-specific precautions
examples: Three sessions with 14 participants were run; scenarios covered standard tracheostomy, small goitre, pneumothorax and intubation difficulty
key_sources: Favier V., Kimmoun A., Gatin A., Gallet P. (2020). Percutaneous tracheostomy simulation training for ENT physicians in the treatment of COVID-19-positive patients. European Annals of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Diseases. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anorl.2020.06.002
